children: lost more than 13% in premarket trading on Wednesday in reaction to the latest data from a Phase 1 study testing its lead candidate micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO) as a late-line option for certain head and neck carcinoma.

Citing an Aug. 18 data cut based on 33 efficacy-evaluable patients, the company said that the antibody-drug conjugate at 5.4 mg/kg was associated with a 36% confirmed objective response rate and a 94% disease control rate.
However, a Nov. 3 data cut from the study indicated last year that MICVO led to a 46% cORR and 92% DCR when administered intravenously once
The study enrolled patients with recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma who had received at least two prior lines of therapy.
Based on 35 safety-evaluable patients, the company said that there were no new safety signals and the tolerability profile of the experimental therapy met its expectations.

The MICVO monotherapy trial is set to generate updated overall survival data in H1 2027. The company set a Q4 2026 timeline to report updated data from its Phase 1/2 combination study testing MICVO in combination with Merck’s

title: Pyxis slides after new early-stage trial data for lead asset in head and neck cancer
